description: Four-output TR8x4(P2) actuator with lightened formed 5052-O panels, matching Ø76/86 metal end discs and four dense, pocketed PETG cover quadrants with local clearance pockets and overlapping seams. Twenty added M3×0.5 metal-panel stand threads follow a five-point sketch referenced to the output axes, with Ø3.4 PETG shank passages. Four motor lead routes and separate reserve grooves connect to the enlarged end ports. Motor positions are unchanged; thin motor/gear zones are intentional open windows.
releaseRequirements: Laser-cut four 3 mm 5052-O panels to their actual cutting patterns. Form two with 90-degree bends in one direction and two in the opposite direction. Use the execution-specific forming and finishing instructions. Use plain Ø10.02 bearing holes without recesses or chamfers; MF106 flanges remain outside the sheet. Finish DIN7991 seats only on the actual motor side; do not add reverse-side seats for unification.

Use annealed O temper for the selected 1.5 mm inside bend radius in 3 mm sheet. Confirm the neutral-axis allowance, rolling direction, tooling and springback on a formed sample; H32 is not an interchangeable tight-bend temper.

Laser-cut two 5052-O end discs 3 mm thick matching the selected Ø76/86 enclosure with through 50×3.15 capsule slots and four Ø10 cable holes on radius 28.5, starting at 15.5 degrees and repeating every 90 degrees. Chamfer cable holes 0.5 mm on both faces. Leave 3.5 mm panel tongues projecting 0.5 mm past the disc faces for welding.

Weld the bare 5052-O panel/end-disc shell before installing the bearing connector, bearings, shafts, nuts, forks, motors or gears. Assign welding fixtures, sequence, distortion control and post-weld seat inspection without changing the specified material.
Keep panel placement frames separate from approved source-drive frames. Preserve the exchanged A/C drives, unchanged B/D drives and negative/positive source-angle signs respectively.
Interlock the upper X wall pair with the lower Y pair through the waist slots, then clamp at the four external corners with M3×10 low-head screws and M3 nuts.
Machine the separate central four-bearing cross as a functional shaft joint. Finish its four MR52 seats and retain the shaft-tip clip access; it is separate from the four main housing panels.
Use 16×12×12 mm nuts with the public source two-start female thread and relieved 15.2 mm engagement. Retain the original 20.606 mm lever, 31 mm working thread and 15 mm travel for ±20 degree outputs.

Retain the public motor-body and TR8 thread geometry, bearings and X=-13 shaft-pin stations; machine the quad screw journals and retaining grooves to the local schedule. Use the local 22-tooth module 1 gears at 22 mm center distance with 5 mm faces shifted 1.6 mm toward the bearings and extended pinned hubs. Mount motors with sourced DIN7991 M3×5 countersunk screws and matching rim/cone seats; retain 2 mm nominal motor insertion.

Machine each one-piece fork with a Ø11 eye and 6 mm straight arm in the same plane, tapering smoothly to the 8.4 mm clevis web and joining both 2.6 mm cheeks. Place the hub/shaft pin station at radius11.1. Drill the Ø2 through guide bore along the arm, then match-drill the shaft fixation joint for the Ø2×10 pin; its eye-entry and web-side recesses are0.5 and8.2 mm respectively.

Fit the outer MF106 bearings at radius 17.6 through plain Ø10.02 panel holes, with their flanges outside the sheet. Turn the output head from radius 19.35 to 24.35, with a Ø19 back to 23.65 and Ø20 front rim. Preserve four M3 PCD14 holes and 0.25 mm nominal bearing/head gap.

Validate the proposed fork and nut side-window loading paths with the closed welded shell. Fork hubs areØ11, cheeks and webs8.4 mm wide; preserve drive centers and theØ2×10 pin station; use the current slot root, mouth, full-thickness straight eye arm, rounded web and lip contours.
Assign bearing fits, interlock clearances, cutter radii, shaft end float, clamp preload, application loads, lubrication and controller limits from the native CAD and finished assembly.

Tap twenty additional M3×0.5 through threads, five per panel: two lateral holes at output-axis level and three centerline holes above it. Use the shared station API. Cut the shallow ears from the same 3 mm blank and retain the original bearing foot and four separate cover threads. Preserve Ø3.4 PETG passages for M3 shanks only; stand-bolt heads remain outside PETG. The stand and its fasteners are not included; no mechanism hardware is added.

Print the actual PETG quadrants with dense perimeters and 100% infill in modeled solid regions. Preserve clearance pockets, overlapping joints and running gaps. Retain intentional motor/gear windows without thin films; the minimum-land requirement applies only to closed regions. Attach at the API stations using four DIN7991 M3×6 screws, one per quadrant, as recorded in the actual BOM. Keep existing motor positions. Verify covered travel and motor/PETG temperatures. No acoustic attenuation or dB rating is assigned without measurement.

Cut the dedicated rounded panel and end-disc lightening contours from the actual DXFs. Preserve the modeled functional-interface lands and retain the separate cable ports. Use the schedule’s exact relief volume and explicitly assumed density for nominal mass-reduction reporting; qualify application loads separately.

Preserve the four inboard motor rear collectors, their assigned end-port grooves and the separate upper/lower reserve routes. Confirm the actual purchased motor lead-exit clock and boot, cable bend limits, strain relief and shared port packing. The routing geometry does not certify a cable count or connector size, and cables and connectors are not included in the BOM.
